Nov 10 : Nscale, a British cloud provider backed by chip giant Nvidia, is considering delaying a $35 billion stock market listing, the Telegraph reported on Tuesday. Executives at the data-centre developer are assessing whether to pause efforts to go public until next year, the report added. Nscale did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. The report comes days after Reuters reported that Microsoft had declined an option to expand its existing agreement with Nscale to rent more computing power at a Texas data center.

The London-based company filed for an IPO in September, when it sought about $3.5 billion in funding, including $2 billion from Nvidia. Nscale plans to list on the NYSE under the symbol "NSCL." The news about Nscale's IPO comes as Anthropic moves ahead with its own listing plans. The AI giant on Tuesday filed an updated prospectus for its IPO, seeking a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, slightly short of some investors' expectations. Anthropic's IPO is seen as a key test of Wall Street's faith in the AI boom it helped ignite.

Nov 10 : South Africa's twice Olympic gold medallist Tatjana Smith is changing her allegiance to the Netherlands, the 29-year-old said on Tuesday, citing her Dutch heritage and greater opportunities for high-performance support. • Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, retired in 2024 but reversed her decision earlier this year with her sights on the LA28 Games • "To South Africa, when I was a little girl, my biggest dream was to represent my country at the Olympics," Smith said in a tearful video statement posted to social media. "I got to live that dream and it gave me more than I could have ever imagined" • Smith, the 200 metres breaststroke gold medallist in Tokyo and 100m breaststroke champion at the Paris Games, holds dual citizenship with the Netherlands. She has said financial difficulties had made her swimming career hard to sustain • "This gives me the opportunity to explore another part of my identity and the heritage that I've never experienced through sport," said Smith, who also has two Olympic silvers. "The opportunity also offers greater high performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career"

Explainer-Ice hockey-From Canada to Germany, what stands in the way of Russia's ice hockey return?

FAST

Nov 10 : Norway have announced their exclusion from the 2027 World Junior Championship, making way for Russia, despite Canada, the host nation, stating it will bar the Russian team from entering the tournament. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ordered ice hockey's governing body on October 30 to admit Russian teams to five championships. Host governments still decide who can enter, and eight of the 16 teams in the men's World Championship say they would refuse to play Russia. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), now led by Germany's Franz Reindl, said it disagrees with the ruling but will comply. CAS found insufficient evidence that security risks justified extending the ban imposed after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said it had been subsequently informed by the IIHF that Norway would be replaced by Russia at the upcoming junior championship as the lowest-ranked team.

The International Olympic Committee on July 7 provisionally lifted its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee and withdrew its recommended restrictions on Russian athletes and teams. It had already urged federations to readmit Russian and Belarusian juniors to individual and team events. Here are the details. WHAT COMES NEXT? As of November 10, the IIHF had yet to announce Norway's relegation publicly. Swiss Ice Hockey said it had received a revised schedule naming Russia. In a statement, the federation said it was consulting with national associations, host authorities, and organisers on how to proceed following the court decision. Sweden has urged the European Commission to tighten visa rules for athletes representing Russia or Belarus. Finland is preparing restrictions on short-term work visas for Russian athletes across sports, Finnish broadcaster Yle reported. CAN RUSSIA ENTER THE HOST COUNTRIES? CAS left open whether Russia could play under a neutral flag. Canadian Sports Secretary Adam van Koeverden, however, said the neutral designation applied to individual athletes. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will not let ice hockey players from Russia or Belarus take part in the World Junior Championship in Alberta in December. Czech Interior Minister Lubomir Metnar said existing rules prevent him from issuing short-stay visas for Russian players for January's women's under-18 championship in Ostrava. Germany's government said opposition from teams and sponsors made staging the men's championship in May with Russia "effectively impossible". Berlin left open the possibility of refusing visas, saying it would assess applications individually. WHICH TEAMS WOULD REFUSE TO FACE RUSSIA? Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Latvia, Norway and Sweden say they would refuse to play Russia. Ukraine qualified for the men's top division for the first time since 2007. Sports Minister Matvii Bidnyi said they intend to compete but would refuse to play Russia.  Switzerland said their juniors will compete in Alberta but would sit out the December 27 game against Russia on the IIHF's revised schedule. HOW HAS RUSSIA RESPONDED? Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that countries opposing rulings to allow Russia to take part in international sport are violating the rights of both Russian athletes and democratic institutions. Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev told Vesti that expecting Russia to withdraw was "the height of hysteria". He called what he described as Swedish fears of psychological trauma "simply idiotic" and said Russia would prove their superiority on the ice. Degtyarev said opponents would forfeit and countries blocking Russia risked losing hosting rights, which the IIHF council can withdraw after a review. He said Moscow would ask the IOC to monitor Canada and Germany. WHY ARE BELARUS STILL EXCLUDED? The CAS ruling covered Russia alone. Belarus have been excluded since the country supported Moscow's invasion. On November 7, the IIHF confirmed Belarus would miss the junior and men's championships, citing existing tournament arrangements. Belarusian federation chairman Alexander Bogdanovich questioned the different treatment. WHAT IS AT STAKE FOR HOSTS AND SPONSORS? The Finnish city of Turku said it will give up co-hosting the 2028 World Juniors in Finland with Tampere if Russia compete. AJ Products, a men's championship sponsor since 1989, has withdrawn from the 2027 tournament. If Russia play, Nokian Tyres will end its sponsorship, Skoda Auto will review its involvement and Strauss will remove its logos while considering a full withdrawal. GENEVA: The Un ited States spurned a UN meeting on Tuesday (Nov 10) where its human rights record un der US President Donald Trump was due to be examined, drawing criticism from rights groups who say violations have surged to levels not seen in decades. Washington disengaged from the Geneva-based UN Human Rights Co un cil last year, citing an anti-Israel bias, and this is the second year in a row that it has skipped its own review - a process that even authoritarian state s take part in. The US left its seat on the stage of the UN meeting empty and the council decided to postpone the event until January. A US State Department spokesperson said participation would imply endorsement of the co un cil's work.

"This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own 'values' as it p us hes anti-American rhetoric," the spokesperson said, without responding to allegations about the US record. The 47-member co un cil has not directly criticised Washington's rights record but its appointed experts have, such as over migrant deportations. Washington said deportations wer e carried out in accordance with US immigration law.

QUESTIONS ON ABORTION AND DEATH PENALTY The Un iversal Periodic Review asks all 193 UN member states to submit a rights report every few years and these are review ed by other states , which provide non-binding recommendations. UN documents show co un tries had planned on Tuesday to raise issues such as abortion and the death penalty. US and international non-governmental organisations also sent nearly 200 UN submissions covering topics from migration to racial discrimination. “We've seen attacks on f un damental human rights and civil liberties un precedented in generations," Jamil Dakwar , of the American Civil Liberties Un ion , told reporters in Geneva. "Enough is enough." Fourteen co un tries are due to take part in the review process in Geneva this month. In Trump's first term in office, the US submitted its UPR report. Noor Abdalla, wife of pro-Palestinian student activist Mahmoud Khalil, who was held in immigration detention last year, is among campaigners pressing UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk to promptly hold a briefing on the US rights situation, even in Washington's absence. "When the most powerful government in the world is not held acco un table, they think that they can do whatever they want," Abdalla told reporters. However, diplomats were sceptical given that few states want to confront Washington. "The view is to leave the door open and hope they come back in two years," said a diplomat.

MADRID, Nov 10 : Spain's government has demanded that TikTok suspend its operations in Spain until it eliminates child sexual abuse material, it said on Tuesday, after a media report documented 1,183 explicit posts on the platform with millions of views. Youth Minister Sira Rego, whose ministry cannot singlehandedly ban the platform in Spain, has appealed to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company, according to a statement by the ministry. "Social media cannot be lawless territory," Rego said. The request comes months after Sanchez's government requested a probe into X, Meta and TikTok for allegedly spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse material, as European regulators intensify scrutiny of big tech over harmful and illegal content.

NEW YORK, Nov 10 : US electricity consumption will rise to record highs in 2026 and 2027 due to power-hungry AI data centers and electrification, the US Energy Information Administration said in its Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) on Tuesday. The EIA projected that power demand will rise from a record 4,216 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) in 2025 to 4,306 billion kWh in 2026 and 4,370 billion kWh in 2027. If correct, 2026 would be the third year in a row of record demand. Demand is surging largely due to data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. Homes and businesses have also been relying more on electricity and less on fossil fuels for heat and transportation. The EIA forecast that power sales in 2026 will rise to 1,546 billion kWh for residential consumers, 1,557 billion kWh for commercial customers and 1,061 billion kWh for industrial customers.

The all-time highs stand at 1,519 billion kWh for residential consumers and 1,503 billion kWh for commercial customers in 2025 and 1,064 billion kWh for industrial customers in 2000. As renewable output rises, the EIA said the share of power generation from coal will slide from 17 per cent in 2025 to 15 per cent in 2026 and 2027, while the share of natural gas in 2026 will hold steady from 2025 at 40 per cent, then ease to 39 per cent in 2027. The percentage of renewable generation will rise from around 24 per cent in 2025 to 25 per cent in 2026 and 28 per cent in 2027, while nuclear power's share will hold at 18 per cent in 2026 and 2027, the same as in 2025, according to the outlook. The EIA projected that gas sales in 2026 would slide to 12.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) for residential consumers and 9.4 bcfd for commercial customers, but rise to 23.8 bcfd for industrial customers and 37.4 bcfd for power generation. Those figures compare with all-time highs of 14.3 bcfd in 1996 for residential consumers, 9.9 bcfd in 2025 for commercial customers, 23.8 bcfd in 1973 for industrial customers, and 36.8 bcfd in 2024 for power generation.

Source: Reuters

Nov 10 : Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev are the first players confirmed to represent Europe at the 2027 Laver Cup in Los Angeles, organisers announced on Tuesday, as the team bids for a record-extending seventh title. The 10th edition of the tournament will take place at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles from September 24-26. Team World is made up of players from outside Europe. The annual tournament, launched in 2017, is intended to be tennis's equivalent of golf's Ryder Cup. World number one Zverev will make a record eighth Laver Cup appearance in Los Angeles, having been part of Team Europe's six title-winning campaigns since making his debut at the inaugural event in Prague in 2017.

Defiant Hegseth blasts impeachment effort ahead of House vote

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth also thanked US President Donald Trump for his support as lawmakers prepared to vote on eight articles of impeachment against him.

WASHINGTON: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday (Nov 10) blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce that would embolden US adversaries, as he lashed out at his political opponents in Congress and the media in an unapologetic defence of his record. Striking a defiant tone at a Pentagon news briefing, Hegseth thanked US President Donald Trump for his continued support as the House of Representatives scheduled a procedural vote for late Tuesday that will test support for his impeachment. Hegseth said past impeachments of Trump had ultimately failed, and added: "Both times he came back stronger, and the American people sent him back to the White House. Now they're trying a third time. This time against a member of his cabinet."

US Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced eight articles of impeachment against H egseth on Monday. Massie said in a post on X that if the House of Representatives can overcome Tuesday's procedural effort, "we will proceed to a real debate and vote on the Articles of Impeachment." Congressional sources say the resolution may have the votes to pass even with Trump’s Republicans still controlling the House until Democrats take over on Jan 3. Conviction appears unlikely in the Senate, however, where a two-thirds majority is required and Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats. Hegseth is accused of various abuses of power in office, including issuing orders to go to war with Iran without an imminent threat or approval from Congress. Voter anger over the Iran war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week's midterm elections . A new Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress to act to end the war with Iran.

US Representative Thomas Massie (R-KY) holds a press conference about his resolution to impeach Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, US, Nov 9, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein)

Vice President JD Vance has publicly questioned the war. Hegseth declined to be drawn into responding to Vance, but defended the conflict, calling Trump courageous and saying Iran's military has been left in ruins. "History will judge the Iran war quite differently than the conventional wisdom right now," he said. Hegseth cited US Secretary of State Marco Rubio as saying of the war: "It's not necessarily popular, but it may have been necessary, and that's certainly how I feel. It was a necessary undertaking." Trump repeated his backing of Hegseth in a post on his Truth Social platform just after the Pentagon briefing ended. "Pete Hegseth gets an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!" he wrote. A polarizing figure in American politics, Hegseth would be the first US defense secretary to be impeached. The last time any civilian leader of the US military was impeached was in 1876, when William Belknap held the title "secretary of war." Hegseth, a former Fox News host, calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and "woke" when he took office last year. But even some Republicans say his strained relations with Congress are becoming a political liability as the administration seeks a US$1.5 trillion defense spending package. In a possible nod to the spending requests, Hegseth said Republicans should use their final weeks in control of Congress to deliver wins for the American people instead of pursuing his impeachment. If he's still around next year, Democrats have promised to investigate Hegseth and his handling of the Pentagon, including his firing of the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and other top military officers.

Nov 10 : Anthropic said on Tuesday it was bringing its Claude assistant to video conference platform Google Meet, as the company pushes to integrate AI deeper into everyday office work. Earlier in the day, Anthropic launched a roadshow for its highly anticipated US initial public offering, with plans to raise as much as $64.4 billion at a $1.02 trillion valuation. The offering will test investors' appetite for the AI boom and Anthropic's massive spending plans. Called Claude Meetings, the new feature will let users add Claude to video calls as a visible participant. Anthropic said Claude would be able to follow the conversation and turn discussions into work in real time, while also drafting plans, creating timelines and answering questions in the call's chat. The feature is designed to shift AI's role in meetings from simply recording or summarizing conversations to doing the work that follows from them while the discussion is still taking place, Anthropic said.

Nov 10 : IBM said on Tuesday that it was ending US visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of roles in IBM Consulting, which employs more than 150,000 people. The move comes amid tight scrutiny of foreign tech hiring by Donald Trump's administration. Last month, it suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several major outsourcers, including Cognizant, Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services, from the Permanent Labor Certification process — a key step toward green cards for foreign workers. IBM Consulting has used US high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages, but participation has been declining for years, a company spokesperson told Reuters. It opted to end sponsorship for most such roles as skill availability and client needs have evolved, the spokesperson added.

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 : Alphabet's Google has agreed to additional privacy protections in the acquisition of employee data from defunct Spirit Airlines, a union representing employees said Tuesday. The agreement clears the way next week for approval of Google's $10 million deal to acquire Spirit data to train AI models. The union said it had won a more rigorous de-identification process than previously planned and added significant employee data will be excluded from the sale, including health and medical information. As part of Spirit's closure and asset liquidation, Google won an auction in August for data from emails, spreadsheets and calendars, as well as for marketing, productivity and operations. Spirit Airlines halted operations in May. A bankruptcy judge is now set to approve the deal next week.

The Association of Flight Attendants-CWA said the de-identified data will also be reviewed by an independent verification agent chosen in consultation with unions, and Google is prohibited from attempting to re-identify the data and is required to process it in a secure environment and treat it as confidential. A group of about 120 lawmakers raised concerns last month about the data sale. Last month, a privacy ombudsman recommended a US bankruptcy judge approve the deal after excluding passenger personal information from 97 million Spirit customers. The lawmakers, led by Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat, and Representative Steven Horsford, a Nevada Democrat, said the sale would include 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages and other employee records. Spirit Airlines said it was pleased to have reached a resolution with labor unions as it continueed to maximize value for its creditors. "We are grateful for the collaboration of Google, the consumer privacy ombudsman, our labor unions, and other key stakeholders who are engaging with us constructively on this sale," a spokesperson said. Google, which did not immediately comment Tuesday, said last month it did not want to acquire personal information. "We are not looking to buy any personal information from Spirit. The information will either be completely excluded or will be de-identified by an independent third party before Google receives any data," Google said last month.

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 : Toyota Motor said on Tuesday it will bring its ultra-compact mini KEI trucks to the US market for fleet customers starting in the second half of 2027 as part of a limited rollout after President Donald Trump encouraged the move. A third of the 3.7 million new cars sold in Japan last year were mini, or "kei", cars — tiny vehicles that are not produced by American automakers. The KEI-01, which has a 660 cc three-cylinder engine and four-wheel drive, will be assembled at Toyota's plant in Indiana. Toyota will add 50 jobs and invest $34 million in the project. The right-hand-drive trucks measure just over 11 feet (3.35 m) in length and under 5 feet in width with a maximum speed of 25 miles per hour (40 kph). Toyota said the vehicle is designed to comply with federal low-speed vehicle safety requirements and initial distribution will focus on fleet customers rather than retail sales. Toyota also said it is relaunching its Scion in the US.

Nov 10 : Mercor said on Tuesday it had raised $750 million in a funding round that valued the AI training startup at $20 billion. The Series D round drew participation from Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, Nvidia and funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, among others. Here are more details: • Investor enthusiasm for AI has fueled a sharp rise in private funding this year, creating a growing group of heavily capitalized startups carrying multibillion-dollar valuations

• Mercor, which began as an AI-powered hiring platform, now connects technology companies with subject-matter experts whose knowledge is used to train, test and improve AI models and agents • The San Francisco-based company said it will use the funding to help train and test AI agents on professional tasks • "Every job in the economy will need its own AI agents and every company will need a way to train and evaluate them on its own work," co-CEO Brendan Foody said • According to Crunchbase, AI-driven startups raised $102 billion, or 64 per cent of global venture capital, in the third quarter of 2026 • Mercor, which is backed by Jack Dorsey and venture capitalist Peter Thiel, was valued at about $10 billion after raising $350 million in October last year

Source: Reuters
